questions: Does body_length 0.24 m lower max_error or steering_oscillation on the s-bend and slalom compared with iteration 4 (0.18 m)?
Does progress on the s-bend move above or below 0.185, and does control_effort rise with the added yaw inertia?
Is the first off-track event still preceded by a steady drift, or does it now come from a sudden loss on the sharpest bend?
Does body length change anything on the oval, where progress was flat across all geometry changes?

intent: Isolate body_length as the geometry lever for yaw inertia. Start from the best measured design (iteration 4, 58.54) and change only body_length from 0.18 to 0.24 m. Sensors, wheel_track, wheel_radius, mass and body_width stay fixed, so the race isolates inertia. Expect max_error and steering_oscillation to fall on the s-bend and slalom if extra inertia damps the drift, with progress holding at or above 0.185.
learning: Iterations 4 to 9 show a plateau near 58. Footprint size (12 vs 16 mm) is neutral, and y=0.03 m is strongly harmful. Wheel_radius and mass are at their measured optima. Body_length is the last untested inertia lever. If it is also neutral, the next geometry question is whether the sensor span should widen to about 0.07 m, and any remaining gain must come from the controller (kp, kd, base_speed), which is the Integrator's domain.
rationale: Evidence across iterations 0 to 9: every run in every iteration ends off_track on all three development tracks. max_error sits on the 0.06 m off-track floor, and progress is stuck between 0.06 and 0.19. Line loss is now rare (oval 0, s-bend about 0.95, slalom about 0.85 at iteration 4), so sensor span is no longer the main limit. The off-track floor is max(0.06, 0.0125 + body_width/4), which is 0.06 m for every allowed body width, so body width cannot help. Scores have plateaued near 58: iteration 4 (16 mm, 58.54) and iteration 9 (12 mm, 58.27) are effectively tied, so the footprint lever is neutral. Wheel_track is at its 0.08 m minimum, and wheel_radius 0.03 m and mass 0.8 kg are near their measured optima. Sensor lead y=0.05 m beat both y=0.03 m (41.1) and y=0.07 m (confounded, 47.8). The one geometry lever not yet tested in isolation is body_length, which sets yaw inertia (mass*(L^2+W^2)/12) without changing the off-track floor or the sensor layout. Iteration 2 lowered inertia and hurt, and iteration 6 raised mass and hurt, so inertia's direction is unclear. I therefore revert to the iteration 4 design (16 mm footprints, which is the marginally better footprint) and change only body_length, from 0.18 m to 0.24 m. That raises yaw inertia by about 1.5x (from about 0.0031 to about 0.0047 kg m^2). Expected result: if inertia damps the drift, max_error and steering_oscillation fall and progress rises above 0.19 on the s-bend. If the score falls or holds, the body is confirmed to be inert, and the plateau is set by controller gain or base speed, which is outside geometry.
